name: Test-L Term 1 Week 2
description: Initial curriculum-derived vocabulary set. Core marks direct weekly vocabulary targets; expanded entries are vocabulary-bearing words extracted from exercises, answer choices, analogies, sentence completion, and vocabulary-in-context material.

words.meaning: to give up a position of power or responsibility
words.example: The king chose to abdicate the throne.

words.meaning: something unusual that differs from what is normal
words.example: The cold summer day was an aberration.

words.meaning: causing strong disgust or hatred

words.meaning: to obey or follow a rule or decision
words.example: Everyone must abide by the rules.

words.meaning: rough or able to scrape; also harsh in manner
words.example: Sandpaper has an abrasive surface.

words.meaning: to choose not to do or have something

words.meaning: a very large amount
words.example: The garden produced an abundance of tomatoes.

words.meaning: extremely bad
words.example: The team had an abysmal first half.

words.meaning: officially approved or recognized
words.example: She attended an accredited school.

words.meaning: organized action meant to create social or political change
words.example: Environmental activism can include community cleanups.

words.meaning: to respect or look at with approval

words.meaning: to warn or scold someone firmly
words.example: The teacher admonished the class for shouting.

words.meaning: deserving strong dislike or disgust

words.meaning: to decide to do without something

words.meaning: to stop something from happening

words.meaning: a strong desire to achieve something

words.meaning: the reason or desire that makes someone act

words.meaning: to point out, show, or suggest

words.meaning: to stop

words.meaning: worth a lot or very useful
